text:
zara: quick thread — proposal to add an explicit `compatibility_vector` field to rollout metadata so routers can make deterministic fallback choices without peeking into model artifacts

sam: curious — is this separate from `variant_hints` or a replacement?

zara: separate. `variant_hints` stays lightweight (perf/quantization hints). `compatibility_vector` encodes API/kv-cache/seqlen compatibilities and semantic fallbacks (e.g., can_fallback_to: [tiny,quantized-8bit])

ashley: examples? a short schema snippet would help.

zara: yeah, thinking small — e.g.
```json
"compatibility_vector": {
  "api_shape": "chat_v2",
  "kv_cache_compatible": true,
  "max_seq_len": 2048,
  "fallback_order": ["redwood-tiny-v1","redwood-quant-8-v2"]
}
```

leo: how does this interact with pinning? if a tenant pins `model:stable-2026` we still need graceful degrade rules.

zara: pin wins for exact model id. but if capacity constrained we use pin policy on the pin object: `allow_compat_fallback: boolean` plus `fallback_constraints` to honor tenant SLAs. router consults pin -> if allow_compat_fallback true then consult compatibility_vector for alternatives

sanjay: what about security/contract surface — some customers won't allow cross-quantization fallbacks for accuracy/regulatory reasons. we need an explicit opt-out.

maria: also add telemetry keys: `compat_reason` and `compat_score` to trace why fallback chosen. otherwise ops will be blind.

zara: agreed. propose metadata additions: `compatibility_vector` (object), `pin_policy` (allow_compat_fallback, required_accuracy_threshold), and `compat_telemetry_keys` (compat_reason, compat_score).

ashley: tiny nit — agents.md and other tooling expect flat rollout tags. adding nested object could break older indexers. maybe represent `compatibility_vector` as a compact string token + registry to expand? e.g. `compat_token: cv:12345`

leo: that would avoid migration pains. token registry can be updated independently. we store token on rollout metadata and registry holds full JSON. router fetches registry when needed (cached).

zara: I like token + registry pattern. keeps metadata small in DB rows and avoids huge JSON blobs in every rollout record.

sam: ops question — if registry is out-of-sync across regions, router might attempt fallback to a model unavailable in that region. need region-scoped tokens or region-aware registry lookup.

zara: yes — token resolution should accept a region param and return region-available alternatives. fallback_order entries should be region-qualified or omitted if not present.

maria: add TTL and version on registry entries so we can rotate tokens safely.

leo: implementability: runtime needs a cache with invalidation hooks from control plane. maybe a pub/sub event when registry changes.

zara: implementation plan: 1) schema PR to rollout metadata to add `compat_token` and `pin_policy` 2) registry service + migration to populate tokens for existing rollouts 3) router changes to resolve tokens with region param and consult `pin_policy` 4) telemetry + tests.

sam: timeline?

zara: aiming for RFC follow-up next week, small schema PR within 2 weeks, registry MVP by end of quarter.

deploy-bot: deploy-notice: schema-PR #512 opened by zara — CI checks running :rocket:

ashley: thanks — in the RFC follow-up please add a couple of example failure modes (token missing, region mismatch) and suggested fallback semantics (deny vs best-effort).

zara: will do. tagging @sam @leo for review on the fallback semantics doc.

sam: ack, will review. :+1:

maria: one more ask — include a simple size-budget guideline for `fallback_order` (e.g., max 10 entries) so registry stays small.

zara: noted. will add budget and TTL details in the writeup.

leo: sounds good. thanks everyone.
